steps.title: Import Vue and ref from 'vue'
steps.instruction: Import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package to use Vue's reactive state management capabilities.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.

steps.hint: Use the ref() function to create a reactive array. You can include URLs like 'https://picsum.photos/400/300?random=1'.

steps.title: Add container structure for images
steps.instruction: In the template section, add a <div> element with the class 'image-container' to wrap the images you'll add later.
steps.hint: Look for the template section and add the div element there. This container will hold multiple images.

successCriteria: The template contains a <div> element with class 'image-container'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the container structure that will hold your lazy-loaded images.

steps.title: Add v-for directive to iterate through images
steps.instruction: Inside the template's image container, add a v-for directive to iterate through the imageUrls array and render an img element for each URL.
steps.hint: Use v-for="url in imageUrls" on the img element to loop through the array.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: v-for directive in Vue
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a v-for directive that will generate multiple img elements when imageUrls is populated.
successCriteria: The image container includes an img element with v-for="url in imageUrls" directive.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the v-for directive to iterate through the image URLs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added v-for="url in imageUrls" to an img element inside the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The v-for directive is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added v-for="url in imageUrls" to an img element.

steps.instruction: Inside the v-for loop, add an img element for each image. Bind the src attribute to the current image URL and add the loading='lazy' attribute.
steps.hint: Use the v-for item variable to access each image URL. The img element should look like .

steps.expectedOutcome: Each image will have an img element with the correct src binding and lazy loading attribute.
successCriteria: The img element is added inside the v-for loop with :src binding to the url variable and loading='lazy' attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the img elements with lazy loading. This tells the browser to defer loading images until they're near the viewport.

steps.title: Wire load event handler to images
steps.instruction: Add the @load event binding to each img element to call the handleImageLoad function when an image loads.
steps.hint: Use the @load directive on the img element and set it equal to your handler function name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring an event handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each image element will now trigger the handleImageLoad function when it finishes loading.
successCriteria: The img elements have an @load attribute set to handleImageLoad.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the image load events to your handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure each img element has @load="handleImageLoad".
steps.feedbackWrong: The img elements don't have the load event handler wired correctly. Add @load="handleImageLoad" to each img element.

steps.title: Display loading status in the UI
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element above the image container that conditionally displays 'Images loaded!' when isLoaded is true, and 'Loading images...' when it's false.
steps.hint: Use Vue's template syntax with a conditional expression (ternary) inside double curly braces to show different text based on the isLoaded reactive state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional text display in Vue

{{ isVisible ? 'Content is visible!' : 'Content is hidden' }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show visual feedback about the image loading status, with the text updating from 'Loading images...' to 'Images loaded!' once all images have loaded.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists with conditional text that displays 'Images loaded!' when isLoaded is true and 'Loading images...' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to display the image loading status, providing clear visual feedback to users.
